title: Canonical NodeDefinition authority body
description: OBJECTIVE: define the immutable per-node execution-contract content required by design lines 199/255, without yet deriving graph-recursive hashes. HARD DEPENDENCIES: task-154ce48d1acc4e868da01bec87304b48 and root publication task-dc21cb4a8f2a4c1c902f3bf3a82a59c2 must be DONE and bare-importable from @moe/scheduler. DELIVERABLE: closed versioned descriptor-safe draft/create/admit/encode/decode surface for a deeply frozen NodeDefinition authority body containing objective, exact derived criterion-content bindings, constraints, capability, normalized read/write scopes, resources, budget request, derived plan-execution binding, verification-recipe revision bindings, repository base, policy-slice hash, join/completion linkage, sorted direct-hard `{edgeKey, DependencyContract}` entries, and exact monotonic-predicate registry proofs. Draft creation receives admitted planning records and derives their graph-independent identities through production @moe/core; it accepts no caller content digest/hash. Reuse validateDependencyContract and persist only its normalized result. Exclude graph/revision IDs, lifecycle, workspace/lease/input/result/attempt state, outgoing consumers and selected witness truth. NOT IN SCOPE: recursive predecessor hashes, GraphRevisionContent, root publication, daemon/store/transport. The recursive-hash task filed next is the production consumer.
definitionOfDone: A closed versioned deeply frozen NodeDefinition authority body covers every nonrecursive design-255 field with bounded objective/ids/arrays, normalized locale-independent `/` scope paths, closed join role, no execution affordance, and explicit rejection of excluded/extra fields.

Creation admits PlanRevision and AcceptanceContract through their production surfaces, derives the graph-independent plan and selected criterion identities, proves node/criterion/recipe applicability, and rejects any caller-supplied plan/criterion digest, nodeAuthorityHash, predecessor hash, graph hash or revision id with exact code+layer.

Each direct-hard entry stores an edgeKey plus the normalized output of production validateDependencyContract; MONOTONIC entries require a durable exact matching predicate-registry proof, conflicting witness bindings refuse, and no registry proof is synthesized or silently demoted.

Canonical encode/decode reject malformed, unsupported, duplicate, unordered, over-limit, noncanonical, dependency/source-layer, proof-registry and digest failures with exact stable code and layer; accepted output is detached and deeply frozen.

Tests use a nonempty real planning/criteria/dependency control, assert positive hostile and authoritative-field roster counts, pin included/excluded fields and exact code/layer, mutation-drill production projectors, verify exact LF bridges and <=250 production sources; `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` prints nonzero counts and records the recursive-hash consumer id.

ARMS, one per DoD-4 noun, each pinning code AND layer as literals:
- malformed: an 8-case hostile sweep with its own generated count — null, a number, a string, an ARRAY of the valid draft, an object whose prototype is not Object.prototype/null, a Proxy over the valid draft, a valid draft carrying an ACCESSOR-backed `objective`, and the bare accessor record. NODE_AUTHORITY_MALFORMED @ NODE_AUTHORITY_ADMISSION. Decode's own malformed arm (a JSON array where the envelope belongs) answers at @ NODE_AUTHORITY_CODEC, so the two layers are distinguished, not conflated.
- unsupported version: TWO arms, because the body and the envelope carry the version separately — body schemaVersion 99 @ NODE_AUTHORITY_SCHEMA, envelope schema tag "MOE-NODE-AUTHORITY/99" @ NODE_AUTHORITY_CODEC.
- duplicate direct-hard edgeKey: NODE_AUTHORITY_DUPLICATE_EDGE @ NODE_AUTHORITY_DEPENDENCIES.
- UNSORTED direct-hard entries: NODE_AUTHORITY_EDGE_ORDER @ NODE_AUTHORITY_DEPENDENCIES on create AND on admit (a sorted body re-admitted with its entries reversed must refuse), with a positive control in between proving the sorted two-entry case admits and keeps ["edge-a","edge-b"].
- over-limit: four at-limit-accepts / one-over-refuses PAIRS (objective bytes, constraint entries, scope entries, dependency entries) sweeping with an asserted count. The dependency arm passes 129 NULL entries, which also pins the ordering convention this package already follows — the raw array ceiling must precede any indexed read, so an over-limit list refuses in constant time rather than being traversed. A fifth arm bounds the persisted proof rationale.
- noncanonical: TWO shapes, a key-reordered body and a whitespace-suffixed encoding, both @ NODE_AUTHORITY_IDENTITY, and the digest-mismatch arm sits immediately before them to pin the ORDER — a swapped VALUE reports DIGEST_MISMATCH, an alternate SPELLING of correct content reports NONCANONICAL. Neither guard subsumes the other, which is what makes the decode-side re-encode compare load-bearing (drill 5's target).
- not-bytes / too-large / unreadable: three separate codes @ NODE_AUTHORITY_CODEC.
- dependency and proof-registry passthrough: already armed in step 2 (validator codes verbatim @ DEPENDENCY_CONTRACT), plus this step's rationale bound.
- detachment: bytes handed to decode are zero-filled AFTER decoding and the decoded body's bytes must be unchanged; the decoded definition is asserted deeply frozen by a recursive walk that returns the PATHS of any unfrozen value, so a failure names the field.

BYTE STABILITY: same admitted inputs twice -> identical bytes; and a 16-probe sweep, one per INCLUDED field family, each asserting the bytes differ from the control, with the probe count asserted (>=16) and tallied. The probes are labelled in the compared string so a failure names the family. Three of them (criterionBindings, planExecutionContentDigest, monotonicPredicateProofs) change only an UPSTREAM record — the acceptance obligation statement, a plan step description, the registry rationale — which is what proves the derived fields are genuinely folded into the digest rather than carried as constants.

SCOPE NORMALIZATION DECISION, recorded because the next slice plans against it: backslash separators NORMALIZE to `/`; duplicate separators collapse; a trailing separator is stripped. CASE IS PRESERVED, NOT FOLDED — `services/API/src` and `services/api/src` are two distinct scopes and both admit. Rationale: case folding is the locale-dependent operation, so folding is what would BREAK design 255's locale-independence promise, and on a case-sensitive filesystem folding would merge two genuinely different scopes into one authority. Locale-independence is instead met by never calling toLowerCase/localeCompare anywhere in the module and sorting by plain code-unit comparison. Refusing (not normalizing): absolute paths, drive-qualified paths, any `..` segment, any `.` segment, and the empty string — five hostile shapes, all NODE_AUTHORITY_SCOPE_INVALID @ NODE_AUTHORITY_SCOPES.

ORDERING DECISION, also recorded for link 3: scalar identifier lists (constraints, resources, verificationRecipeRevisions) and the scope lists are NORMALIZED — deduped and sorted by the producer — because their canonical form is either derived (scopes must be sorted AFTER separator normalization, so a caller cannot pre-sort them) or a pure set. `directHardDependencies` is the one list the producer REFUSES rather than reorders: its values are contracts a separate authority normalized, and the recursive-hash consumer binds the edge order, so silently accepting two orderings as one body would make that binding ambiguous.

WHAT LANDED
- Closed versioned body, NODE_DEFINITION_KEYS = 18 alphabetical keys, which IS the canonical serialization order (one list, so a field cannot be declared without being hashed).
- Derivation is genuine composition through the BARE @moe/core root: encodePlanRevision -> decodePlanRevisionBytes and encodeAcceptanceContract -> decodeAcceptanceContractBytes round-trip the caller's records through core's OWN admission (which also digest-checks them), then derivePlanExecutionContent / deriveAcceptanceCriterionContent produce the two graph-independent identities. Core refusals travel out with core's code under layer PLANNING_SOURCE.
- Each direct-hard entry stores {edgeKey, contract} where `contract` is validateDependencyContract's NORMALIZED output verbatim. Validator refusals travel out with the validator's code under layer DEPENDENCY_CONTRACT.
- THE DEMOTION GUARD (DoD 3). The validator returns ok:true and silently rewrites stability MONOTONIC -> REVOCABLE when no registry proof matches. composeEdges reads the CALLER-STATED stability off the same data property the validator read and refuses NODE_AUTHORITY_MONOTONIC_PROOF_MISSING @ NODE_AUTHORITY_PROOFS when the two disagree. The matched registry entry is then PERSISTED in the body, and re-admission feeds those persisted proofs back to the validator AS the registry — so admission needs no external registry, and a body that lost its proof demotes inside the validator and is caught by the identical guard. One code path for create and for admit.
- Layer stays module-private (`const LAYER_NAMES`, exported `type NodeAuthorityLayer`). tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts:365 would otherwise ratchet on a column-0 `export const *_LAYER(S)` and those files are outside this task.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW FOUND FOUR REAL DEFECTS IN MY OWN CODE; ALL FOUR FIXED BEFORE COMMIT:
1. DEAD GUARD. createNodeDefinition ran the exact-key check BEFORE the forbidden-identity check, so a top-level nodeAuthorityHash answered NODE_AUTHORITY_MALFORMED and the specific NODE_AUTHORITY_CALLER_DIGEST_FORBIDDEN branch was unreachable. Reordered, and a new arm covers it. Drill 8 (move the check back) reddens it.
2. ENCODE COULD MINT BYTES DECODE REFUSES. accept() enforced no ceiling, but decode refuses over NODE_AUTHORITY_LIMITS.maxBytes. The dependency validator alone admits 128 witnesses plus 128 invalidation facts PER contract, so an admissible body can serialize past 1 MiB - encode would succeed and decode would then refuse TOO_LARGE. The ceiling now runs in accept() and refuses NODE_AUTHORITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED @ NODE_AUTHORITY_LIMITS. New arm builds 40 heavy contracts to cross it, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL at 4 contracts that must still encode, so the test cannot pass by refusing everything. Drill 7 reddens it.
3. PROXY-ARRAY ADMISSION. readDerived, requirementsOf and matchProof used Array.isArray, which returns true for a Proxy over an array and whose traps then run during iteration. All three now use this package's isPlainArray, which rejects proxies. Zero Array.isArray remain in the module.
4. A THROW WHERE A REFUSAL BELONGS. canonicalText throws a TypeError on an unrepresentable leaf; that would have escaped create/admit as a crash rather than a coded refusal (rail 4). accept() now catches and refuses NODE_AUTHORITY_MALFORMED @ NODE_AUTHORITY_CODEC, the same defensive shape graph-content.ts uses.
Considered and judged not a risk, recorded so QA need not re-derive it: no concurrency surface at all (pure functions, no IO, no shared mutable state, the module-level TextEncoder/TextDecoder are stateless); readBytes copies before checking the ceiling, which doubles peak memory for a hostile buffer - left as is because the graph-content sibling has the identical order and consistency matters more than the marginal gain.
